scope: Navegação progressiva antes da prioridade; percurso institucional por opções de seleção, sugestões conforme desafios e detalhes livres opcionais. Faixas de tamanho da rede e estados de custo sem inventar quantidades ou valores. Painel, plano e PDFs consistentes; textos e respostas anteriores preservados.

interface: Before priority selection, navigation exposes only Context, Country and Priorities; no future stages, live procurement panel, matrix or calculator.
After AI governance selection, navigation reveals the institutional path. Direct access to dependent steps before priority selection returns to Priorities.
Governance diagnosis was completed with clicks only; visible text boxes counted zero. Suggestions for results reflect selected regulation and child-safety challenges.
Instruments, evidence types, owners, gaps, actions, resources, capacity and review use selection presets; free text is inside Add more information +.
Optional note remains in the plan when the selected situation changes; stored earlier free text is preserved.
Network ranges are selectable and do not become exact counts. Unknown cost, explicit zero and optional informed amounts remain distinct.

pdf.text: Selected labels, network ranges and optional synthetic note appear without internal option IDs or fabricated monetary totals.
pdf.visual: All eight pages rendered and inspected without overlap or clipping.

regressions: Preset IDs retain their meaning after challenge changes.
JSON round-trip preserves selections, custom notes and previous answers.
A governance case can answer every step by selecting options without typing, while unknown costs remain pending.
Selected option labels follow the current language; personal notes retain their text.

bamanankan: Nomes existentes preservados; introduções novas usam fallback inglês explícito, com aviso de tradução preliminar mantido.

interface: Local isolated browser: four governance challenges selected without a limit; Next goes to the institutional diagnosis, with no tool trial screens.
Governance navigation: Context, Institutional diagnosis, Action plan and resources, Monitoring and review.
Budget: entering 1234.56 shows the same formatted subtotal in the resource question, live panel and plan, alongside six missing amounts.
Mixed priorities remain institutional until the user explicitly identifies an AI use project. Separate project and governance buttons preserve each front.
The tool project report uses the identified project title and excludes governance challenge IDs from its projection. Returning to governance preserves its budget.
National school/student totals are formatted by locale; the currency already associated with entered governance amounts is retained if the country changes.
regressions: Sandbox only for G15; saved sandbox data retained when the challenge is unselected.
All selected challenges create actions; existing G1-G10 IDs remain supported, along with other challenge text.
National totals and governance budget cannot change tool project costs.
New institutional answers, previous tool answers, stage data and saved position survive JSON export/import.
Unknown costs are not zero; zero, partial totals, complete totals and invalid imported amounts are distinguished.

pdf.fixture: Synthetic case with regulation and child safety challenges; one amount 1234.56 and six unknown amounts
pdf.text: Numbers and labels match the institutional model; no pilot, PoC, license or procurement annex text in the governance PDFs.
pdf.visual: All pages rendered and inspected; no overlap or clipping.

governance_translation_status: PT/EN/ES/FR new text; existing translations retained for AR/ZH/BM/ZU/SW, with explicit English entries for new text awaiting native review and the existing preliminary-translation notice.
governance_input_style: Selectable presets; Add more information + for optional details.
network_input: Selected ranges or optional exact totals; no conversion of ranges to estimated totals.
cost_input: Unknown, explicit no cost, or optional informed amount; no monetary presets fabricated.
